title: Just AI Governance and the Forbidden-Boundary Principle
abstract: arXiv:2611.13007v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly shapes consequential decisions, yet predictive accuracy is not a sufficient justification for delegated authority. This conceptual study develops an integrated framework for assessing just AI across normative, data, model, and governance layers. Drawing on plural theories of justice, sociotechnical fairness research, and publicly available governance standards, it maps six justice requirements to observable evidence, decision rights, and remedies. It proposes a two-stage evaluation rule: exclude uses that fail independently justified minimum rights constraints, then compare eligible alternatives across multiple performance and governance criteria. As an explicitly limited normative analogy, Genesis chapter 2 motivates a Forbidden-Boundary Principle (FBP), under which an AI agent must not execute externally consequential actions outside pre-authorized boundaries. translated_title: 公正的AI治理与禁越边界原则
translated_abstract: 人工智能日益影响着重大的决策，然而仅凭预测准确性并不足以为委托给AI的决策权提供正当性。本概念性研究构建了一个综合性框架，从规范层、数据层、模型层和治理层四个维度评估AI的公正性。该研究借鉴了多元正义理论、社会技术公平性研究以及公开可用的治理标准，将六项正义要求映射到可观察的证据、决策权和救济措施之上。研究提出了一个两阶段评估规则：首先排除那些未能满足独立论证的最低权利约束的用途，然后在多个性能与治理标准之间比较符合条件的替代方案。作为一项明确限定的规范性类比，《创世记》第二章启发了“禁越边界原则”：根据该原则，AI代理不得在预先授权的边界之外执行具有外部影响的行为。由此产生的第一性原理安全……
tldr: 本文提出了一个涵盖规范、数据、模型与治理四层的公正AI评估框架，将六项正义要求映射到证据、决策权与救济上，并提出两阶段评估规则以及“禁越边界原则”——即AI代理不得在预先授权的边界之外执行具有外部影响的行为。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an integrated four-layer framework for assessing just AI—mapping six justice requirements to evidence, decision rights, and remedies—and introduces a two-stage evaluation rule together with the Forbidden-Boundary Principle, under which AI agents must not execute externally consequential actions beyond pre-authorized boundaries.
